mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by Laves phase particles

evidence.quote: Fe2Nb-type Laves phase particles pinned the grain/subgrain boundaries of deformed grains, leading to mixed microstructures consisting of recovered and recrystallized grains.
The effects of Mo and Nb additions on the microstructure and mechanical properties of two FeCrAl alloys were studied.
The effects of Mo and Nb additions on the microstructure and mechanical properties of two FeCrAl alloys were studied.

The composition of large particles (~ 3 μm, annealed for 504 h at 950 °C) was determined by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy in SEM to be Fe58Nb22Cr9Si6Al5, which confirms that these particles were Fe2Nb-type Laves phase.
Fe2Nb-type Laves phase particles pinned the grain/subgrain boundaries of deformed grains, leading to mixed microstructures consisting of recovered and recrystallized grains.
The grains in FeCrAl-0.7Nb stayed fairly stable at 950 °C. Very little grain coarsening was observed after 24 h at 950 °C
